correctness.rationale: The initiating source proves B=A+A^T has rank 3, T-I=-A^{-T}B, and adj(B)=D(A)pp^T with primitive integral p. Since A is upper unitriangular, left multiplication by -A^{-T} is unimodular and preserves the integral cokernel. For a rank-three 4x4 integral matrix, the torsion order is the gcd of all 3x3 minors, equivalently the gcd of adjugate entries. Primitivity of p makes gcd_{i,j}(p_i p_j)=1, so that order is D(A). Exact exhaustive minor calculations on the five table representatives give determinant divisors (1,1,22), (1,1,40), (1,3,54), (2,4,64), and (1,1,72), hence the stated Smith groups.

value.rationale: The Euler degree D(A) is the central arithmetic invariant used by the source to separate all five mutation classes. The new result identifies that scalar with the torsion size of a natural integral coinvariant quotient and refines it to the complete finite abelian torsion group. The distinction is substantive: the degree-54 and degree-64 classes have noncyclic torsion, information invisible in the scalar degree, while the statement uniformly includes the new degree-72 noncommutative class.
